study.notes: STUDY: single centre randomised open label controlled trial, exenatide twice daily versus insulin aspart 30 twice daily in type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled on oral agents, 66 randomised 1:1, full analysis set 27 versus 32, 52 weeks; primary endpoint carotid intima media thickness. This is the parent trial of group 149, the renal secondary analysis held under decision D-X8, and the two share this trial_id. The secondary endpoint table prints the mean change from baseline per arm with SD and a between arm p (route arm_sds), and Table 1 supplies the baseline arm means for the percent scale. The LDL baseline row of Table 1 is identical to the triglyceride row in both arms (2.18 plus or minus 1.50 and 2.10 plus or minus 1.49), which cannot be correct for both, so the LDL row is entered without a baseline and stays unconvertible rather than being scaled by a denominator that is probably a copy of another row. Brain natriuretic peptide (minus 103.55 plus or minus 39.47 versus minus 84.11 plus or minus 27.95 pg/mL) is BNP, not NT-proBNP, a different analyte on a different scale, and is not entered. 8-hydroxydeoxyguanosine, fibrinogen, irisin and uric acid are outside the inventory. dose_mg 0.01 is 10 ug per injection under the brief's convention for twice daily exenatide. pct_weight_change from the printed weight change, minus 2.21 kg on a baseline of 68.68 kg equals minus 3.2 percent (insulin plus 1.57 kg on 66.30 kg, plus 2.4 percent; the table prints p below 0.01 for the between arm difference but no numeric contrast). No funding statement names a manufacturer (industry_funded FALSE); rob_overall some_concerns

json.design: single centre randomised open label controlled trial, exenatide twice daily versus insulin aspart 30 twice daily, 66 patients with type 2 diabetes, 52 weeks, carotid intima media thickness primary
json.reason: full text group (Europe PMC); eight inventory markers with the mean change per arm and SD in the secondary endpoint table, taken by route arm_sds, with Table 1 baselines as denominators except for LDL

rob.justification: randomised 1:1 but with a sex imbalance (19 of 27 men versus 14 of 32, p 0.038) and a 5 mmHg diastolic difference at baseline (D1 some concerns); open label comparison of an injected incretin with twice daily premixed insulin (D2 high); 66 randomised and 59 in the full analysis set without a flow account in this report (D3 some concerns); laboratory and ultrasound measures with blinded reading of the primary (D4 low); the inventory markers are secondary to a carotid imaging primary, and Table 1 contains an evident copy error in the LDL row (D5 some concerns)

doubts: the Table 1 LDL baseline is identical to the triglyceride baseline in both arms, an evident copy error; the LDL row is therefore entered without a denominator and stays unconvertible
brain natriuretic peptide is reported with large within arm falls in both arms (minus 103.55 and minus 84.11 pg/mL) but is BNP rather than NT-proBNP and is not entered
group 149, the renal secondary analysis of this trial, is held under decision D-X8; if that decision admits stratified tables, its rows must carry this trial_id
pct_weight_change minus 3.2 percent is arithmetic from the printed change and baseline and is expected to be flagged by the numbers check
